note.text: Synonyms have similar meanings in an appropriate context, but are not interchangeable in every phrase. Antonyms express opposition along a relevant dimension. Homophones share pronunciation in the selected model while differing in meaning and often spelling. Homonym terminology varies: here a homonym shares spelling and pronunciation but has distinct unrelated meanings. State the convention and use the sentence to distinguish senses.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to choose a lexical relationship in context and preserve meaning when substituting. Builds on: word formation and model sound contrasts. Leads to: narrative retelling and confusing words.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern
sections.text: Synonyms have similar meanings in an appropriate context, but are not interchangeable in every phrase. Antonyms express opposition along a relevant dimension. Homophones share pronunciation in the selected model while differing in meaning and often spelling. Homonym terminology varies: here a homonym shares spelling and pronunciation but has distinct unrelated meanings. State the convention and use the sentence to distinguish senses.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original models: a rapid response and a quick response are close in this context. Open contrasts with closed for the door’s state. Flour and flower are model homophones; a bat used in a game and a bat as an animal illustrate our narrow homonym convention. Sound patterns can vary by accent, while context still helps identify intended meaning.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Identify the meanings in their actual sentences. Test a replacement for sense, register and collocation. For sound relationships use the stated model and seek oral demonstration; a printed choice alone is not listening assessment.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: Every synonym works in every phrase and register. Correction: Meaning and collocation depend on context.
Any unrelated word is an antonym. Correction: Opposition needs a shared dimension.
Different spelling always guarantees different sound. Correction: Spelling and pronunciation do not correspond uniquely.
The lesson’s narrow homonym convention must be universal. Correction: Dictionaries and courses can use broader terminology.
